comment: What the Excel packages have nowhere to put, in two sections: "fields", the fields a diya-gl line carries, and "bookFields", the paths a book.toml carries. Both name a reach and what the sheets do instead, and EQ2 counts both apart from what the export simply drops, so a real loss is never confused with a structural absence. An entry leaves this file when a sheet gains a cell for it and the writer fills it -- verify-roundtrip.js throws on a declaration that no longer matches anything, so a stale entry cannot sit here counting for nothing.
fieldsComment: One entry per line field. An entry names its reach with exactly one of "products" (every block of that product) or "blocks" (only the named product/block pairs, block being a line's own scope key from verify-roundtrip.js's lineScopeBlock() -- ordinarily its sourceJournalID, except a bank block opening-balance line, which scopes to "bank-opening-balance" so a declaration can name it without blanking the ordinary bank rows sharing its sourceJournalID); a field can carry several entries, e.g. one product-wide and one block-scoped for a different product, as long as no single entry mixes the two.

fields.reason: The Taxi Fixed Assets vehicle block takes a date, a description, a reference and a cost, with no cell for an asset identifier, and the purchase row that buys the asset carries no reference back to the block.

The BST and Taxi single-file templates carry no contractors column on either journal. The SE and Ltd packages keep both sides of the scheme: the tax withheld from a sub-contractor on the purchases journal's CIS certificates column, and the tax a contractor customer withheld on the sales journal's CIS tax deducted column.
The contractors columns take the tax withheld as an amount. The rate behind it is not entered.
A Payslips payroll row is keyed by the employee's name; the payroll id lives on the Employee sheet's own block and is exported to the book's employees table instead of onto each line.
The single-file templates have no Payslips workbook.
The single-file templates have no Payslips workbook.
The single-file templates have no Payslips workbook. Wages reach them as a coded purchase, which carries the amount and nothing else about the pay run.
HPfinance.xlsx holds one agreement at a time and the purchase rows that settle it carry no reference back to it.
The single-file templates have no Payslips workbook.
The single-file templates have no Payslips workbook.

The bank account's opening balance is a bare amount in A1 with no reference cell beside it (the same finding as its missing date: nothing on the tab ties a reference to that figure). An ordinary receipt or payment row keeps its own reference column, so this leaves those rows matching.
The sales and purchases sheets take one kind of document each, so no row says which kind it is. The opening journal keeps its own documentType.
A transaction sheet numbers its rows by position, not by an entry number a row carries, so the export gives each line a fresh number. The number a line went in with is not held.
The single-file sales and purchases sheets carry a customer or supplier name and an invoice reference, and no description column beside them.

The Payslips payroll row carries the employee name as detailComment and the pay figures beside it; the payslip block has no spare column left for a free-text line comment. Sales and purchases keep their own description column, so this leaves those blocks matching.

The bank account's opening balance is a bare amount in A1; the only text anywhere near it is the tab's own row caption ("< Opening Bank Balance", shared string, identical on every account's tab), not a per-line comment. An ordinary receipt or payment row keeps its own comment column, so this leaves those rows matching.
The opening balance sheet is a grid of figures, not a numbered journal, so the export numbers its lines by the order it reads the cells in.
No transaction sheet carries a second free-text column beside the quantity.

Ltd keeps mileage on expensesform.xlsx, which the journal does not post to, and no other column on a Ltd sheet takes a quantity. The SE sales and purchases sheets both carry a mileage column and the export reads the distance back off each of them.

A Ltd sheet's quantity columns are headed with the unit they take, so a row states no unit of its own. The BST, Taxi and SE exporters all read a mileage column back and state "miles" on the line themselves.

The Taxi Sales and Purchases tabs keep no Bank or Cash column: the column the Basic Sole Trader sheets give the payment label is the taxi expense code letter's. The Basic Sole Trader export reads its own column back, coarse-mapping the sheet's free text to "cash" or "bank-transfer".

The SE and Ltd sales and purchases sheets keep no settlement column of their own: how an invoice was paid reaches the package as a separate row on the Bank.xlsx or Cash.xlsx receipts and payments blocks, which the export reads back as its own bank-journal line rather than a flag on the sale or purchase it settles.
VAT is a single book-wide rate cell on the first month's Sales tab, not a code a row carries. The exported taxRate restates that book rate.

VAT is one book-wide rate, entered as a percentage on the first Sales month tab, so no row carries a rate of its own. SE and Ltd restate that book rate on every line; the single-file templates have no rate cell at all.

bookFieldsComment: One entry per book.toml path a product's package cannot hold. The path is the dotted form flattenBook() writes, with empty brackets standing for every index of an array of tables (debtors[].invoice covers debtors[0] through debtors[n]) and "*" standing for a whole segment a table keys on something else (accounts.sales.*.diya-gl:column covers every sales account). "products" names every product the absence applies to; an entry that matches nothing a run left out throws, so a declaration cannot outlive the absence it describes.

bookFields.reason: The chart of accounts is what the package itself declares: the accounts its rows post to, plus the categories a transaction sheet heads an analysis column for. A fixed asset class the opening balance sheet leaves at nil reaches neither -- the opening journal skips a nil cell, and no sheet heads a column per balance sheet account -- so the account leaves nothing behind to name.

The dividends account carries no opening balance and no analysis column of its own: the year's dividend reaches the trial balance from the board minute, not from a coded row, so nothing on the sheets names the account it posts to.

A liability the opening balance sheet leaves at nil is skipped by the opening journal, and the balance sheet heads no column per account, so an account with no opening figure and no coded row leaves nothing behind to name.

The Basic Sole Trader Sales tab totals every income account in one Gross Sales Value column (F), with start-up grants beside it in G, and heads no analysis column per account. A row's own account travels in the carrier column instead, which is not a column the sheet totals.

The Basic Sole Trader Debtors & Creditors sheet names nobody. It is a monthly outstanding table: two entered cells for what was owed when the year opened (C3 and F3, under the "Owed start year" labels), then one row a month whose amount is the template's own formula over that month's Sales or Purchases tab, and a column total under it. No column on the sheet takes a counterparty, an invoice reference, a per-entry amount or an opening/closing timing. What the package does hold of the ledger is the two opening totals, which the export carries as openingBalances.tradeDebtors and openingBalances.tradeCreditors.

No sheet records when the book was written. The Admin dates are the accounting period's start and end, and a workbook's file timestamps are not part of what the workbook says.

The Payslips Employee block's director flag and NI category share one cell: marking a director enters "D" there in place of the category letter, so a director's own category is not on the sheet to read back.
The Payslips Employee block carries a surname, forenames, a national insurance number, a start date, a pay frequency, a payroll number and an NI category. It has no cell for a job title.

The self-employment return carries the basis as a tick box ("If you used traditional accounting rather than cash basis to calculate your income and expenses, put 'X' in the box"). An unticked box means the cash basis and an unfinished form alike, so a blank states nothing to read back.
Company accounts are drawn up on the accruals basis by law, so the Company package's sheets carry no basis cell at all.
The purchases journal keeps a CIS certificates column for the tax withheld from a sub-contractor. No sheet carries a flag for the company's own registration under the scheme.
The Taxi Driver Business Details sheet labels a unique taxpayer reference and nothing else about the trader's own identity; no sheet in the package takes a national insurance number.
The two single-file templates have no VAT rate cell. Their Sales tabs total a gross sales value with no rate beside it, so nothing on any sheet says whether the business charges VAT.

The Taxi Business Details sheet writes only the trader's name (C5), the trade description (C8), the postcode (C17) and the UTR (O5); the address line has no cell of the form's own and stays in the book only.

The Business Details sheet takes a name, a description, an address, a town and a postcode, with no telephone box; and these two products ship no Salesinvoice workbook, whose letterhead is where the multi-file packages keep the number.
The Taxi Business Details sheet writes only the trader's name (C5), the trade description (C8), the postcode (C17) and the UTR (O5); the town has no cell of the form's own and stays in the book only.
The field names the authority a return is filed with. Every one of these packages files with HMRC by construction and no sheet states it, so there is nothing on the workbook to read it back from.

The self-employment return prints the unique taxpayer reference from a pair of boxes on the Business Details sheet ("SE Short"!O8 and R8 read O5 and R5), each holding part of it. The sheet states nowhere how the reference divides between the two, so two halves do not join back into the one reference the book declares.

The Company Stock sheet takes a physical count against each month end and reads its own opening value off the opening balance sheet (D6 = OpenAccounts!E15). The opening stock is that balance sheet figure, which the export carries as openingBalances.stock; the Stock sheet states none of its own.

The year file's annual_investment_allowance is the relief scale HMRC allows (1.00 = full relief up to the cap), not the schema's cap in pounds. The cap itself has no home in the app/data file the package was generated from, so reconstructing it would mean assuming today's figure.
The self-employment year files declare one writing_down_allowance rate. The special rate pool is a Company distinction their capital allowance block does not draw.
No app/data year file carries a count of associated companies: it is a fact about the group a company sits in, not a rate the generator applied.

app/data/ltd-<year>.toml carries corporation tax, employer NI and capital allowances. Income tax is the shareholder's, not the company's, and the Company year files declare none of its rates or bands.
